confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer prices on aggregated cost-of-living sites found in one web search. Those sites gave an inexpensive meal at about USD 3.4-4, a cappuccino at about USD 1.5-2.1, local draft beer at about USD 0.9-1.0 and mid-range dinner for two at about USD 20-30. I raised these a little to allow for the July 2026 pricing window and higher prices in tourist areas such as El Rodadero and the historic centre. I did not search for cocktail or wine prices. Those two are estimates based on the usual Colombian pattern, where imported wine and spirit-based cocktails cost several times as much as local beer, so they are less certain. Accommodation figures are my own general estimates, based on Santa Marta being a busy backpacker and domestic-tourism hub. I did not check booking sites, and July is a holiday period, so rooms may cost more than shown. The FX figure is the latest RBA observation reported by search results (18 November 2026, 0.6720 USD per AUD). I did not open and check the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Comparable to Cartagena (cheaper overall) and Medellín for food prices, and to other Colombian Caribbean coastal tourist towns for accommodation.
